rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7277 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REHABILITATION, SELF-DEVELOPME NT AND SELF-RELIANCE OF DISABLED PERSONS AND THEIR INTEGRATION INTO THE MAINSTREAM OF SOCIETY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  As stated in Republic Act No. 7277 or the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons, persons with disabilities must be assisted and integrated in society. In this light, it is just appropriate for society to facilitate for their participation insociety. However, their willingness to paricipate in society is hampered by difficulties brought about by their disabled condition. However, it must be ensured that this law is effectively implemented and it should penetrate well to the sector of persons with disabilities. This bill then proposes that in every province and municipality, a center must be established that is accessible for all persons with disabilities.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05355

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 198, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE PROVINCIAL WATER UTILITIES ACT OF 1973'
rows.abstract: The amendment to Section 2 of PD No. 198 states: > RELIABLE, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND WATER AND WASTEWATER DISPOSAL SYSTEMS SHALL BE PROVIDED TO AS MANY POPULATION CENTERS OF THE PHILIPPINES AS MAY BE FEASIBLE AND SUSTAINABLE WITH INTEGRATED FACILITIES THROUGH LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS THAT ARE EXISTING OR MAY HEREINAFTER BE FORMED. THE WATER DISTRICTS SHALL BE ORGANIZED TO BE AUTONOMOUS , LOCALLY CONTROLLED, WITH PUBLIC AND/OR PRIVATE CAPITAL, AND OPERAATED AS EFFICIENTLY AS POSSIBLE IN THE FORMAND MANNER AS MAY BE MOST APPPROPRIATE TO THE LOCAL CIRCUMSTANCES TO EXTEND THE BENEFITS OF MUNICIPAL WATER SYSTEMS TO AS WIDE AS SEGMENT OF THE NATION AS POSSIBLE, AND AT THE EARLIEST TIME, THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT SHALL FUND, ADMINISTER AND CHANNELFINANCIAL, TECHNICAL, AND OTHER FORMS OF ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS THROUGH A NATIONAL ENTITY WHICH SHALL ALSO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR AND HAVE AUTHORITY TO PROMULGATE AND ENFORCE RULES AND REGULATIONS TO ASSURE THE EVOLUTION OF WATER DISTRICTS I
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-08-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT PREVENTING AND PENALIZING MONEY LAUNDERING AND ESTABLISHING THE ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING ADVISORY GROUP
rows.abstract: It is the objective of this Act to penalize money laundering, a scheme resorted to by perpetrators of organized crimes and criminal syndicates to hide the proceeds of their illegal activities, by strengthening the legal tools in the evidence-gathering process, establishing enforcement programs to combat it, and providing penal sanctions and remedies to deal with money laundering activities.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03083

rows.title_short: Amending Section 29 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 139, otherwise known as the Judiciary Reorganization Act of 1980
rows.abstract: This bill aims to provide access to higher education for the poor through the creation of a National Student Loan Board, an extension on a nationwide basis of the cross-subsidy program of the University of the Philippines known as the Socialized Tutition and Financial Assistance Program (STFAP). > Specifically, monthly contributions shall be made by persons within specific income brackets that will go into a National Students Loan Fund. These contributions will be graduated, say from one-half percent to four percent of income, according to income bracket.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09276) enacted on 2004-03-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES AS ACTS OF ECONOMIC SABOTAGE
rows.abstract: This bill declares the folloaing as ACTS OF ECONOMIC SABOTAGE:  (1) Smuggling - Outright importation of goods without the corresponding documents for the purpose of evading taxes and duties due pursuant to the provisions of Section 104 of the Customs and Tariff Code, as amended; (2) Technical Smuggling - The importation of goods by falsification of classification of the tariff headings in the import and release documents for the purpose of paying duties and taxes lower than those prescribed bythe Tariff and Customs Code; (3) Misclassificati on of Importation - Importation of goods and materials using documents declaring such goods other than as properly classified in the Tariff and Customs Code; (4) Dumping - Importation of goods and mateerials at prices below the commercial prices in the source country, as defined in Sec. 301 of the Tariff and Customs Code of the Philippines; and (5) Other Unfair Trade Practices - Any other act of importation resulting in reduction of taxes and duti
rows.status: Substituted by HB06530

This bill outlaws the following: (1) Illegal access to computers, computer systems, computer networks, computer servers, and database; (2) Obtaining information on the financial records of a customer of a financial institution without the proper authorization: (3) Obtaining, publishing, and giving out the password to another persons's account; and (4) Unleasing computer viruses.

rows.abstract: This bill proposes to ADD the following paragraph to Article XV PD No. 1."THE INSTITUTE IS HEREBY AUTHORIZED TO IMPOSE FEES, CHARGES, OR OTHER DUES AS IT MAY DEEM APPROPRIATE FROM THOSE WHO VISIT OR USE THE FACILITIES OF THE INSTITUTE'S HISTORIC MONUMENTS AND SHRINES, OR FROM THOSE FROM THE PRIVATE SECTOR WHO AVAIL OF THE INSTITUTE'S RESEARCH, CONSERVATION, OR OTHER SERVICES. THE FUNDS RAISED AS A RESULT THEREOF SHALL BE USED EXCLUSIVELY BY THE INSTITUTE TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN SAID HISTORIC SHRINES OR FOR SUCH OTHER PURPOSES AS MAY BE MANDATED BY LAW."

rows.abstract: "Attrition" is the reduction of personnel as a result of resignation, retirement, dismissal in accordance with laws, death or transfer to another office. Within five (5) years from the approval of this Act, no appointment shall be made fo fill vacated career positions in any government office as a result of attrition. >The system of attrition shall cover the National Government and all its instrumentaliti es or agencies including government-owne d and/or controlled corporations, and governmentfinancial institutions receiving subsidies from the national government.

It likewise proposes additional power for the NEA Administrator to oversee a peaceful and orderly election in each of the RECs' boards.

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ENFORCED OR INVOLUNTARY DISAPPEARANCE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Enforced or involuntary disappearance is committed when a person is arrested, detained or abducted against his/her will or otherwise deprived  of his/her liberty by officials or employees of any branch, subdivision, agency or instrumentality of Government, or by organized groups or private individuals acting on behalf of, or with the support, direct or indirect, consent or acquiescence of the Government, and who subsequently disappeared for at least 48 hours. > This bill aims to penalize the commission of the act of enforced or involuntary disappearance in the country. Further, it also aims to deter, if not totally eradicate the commission of this heinous act by any officer or agent of the State and thus ensure that no person shall be deprrived of life, liberty or property without due process of law, nor shall any person de denied the equal protection of the laws.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-08

rows.abstract: Rationale: The need for policy research and strategic studies could not be more compelling than at the present time. Domestic and international, political, economic, and other developments of profound significance present tremendous challenges to the country. > Strategic studies work has to be done by a group of select scholar-members who, among other things, shall (1) conduct strategic research on national and international concerns; (2) formulate various policy options on various national concerns; and (3) recommend the appropriate actions to support such policies and strategies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-08-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STABILIZE THE SUGAR INDUSTRY BY ESTABLISHING THE SUGAR INDUSTRY RESEARCH AND STABILIZATION FUND AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Twenty percent (20%) of the total Value Added Tax (VAT) proceeds collected on sugar and sugar by-products shall, accrue to and form part of a special fund for the sugar industry which shall be made available solely to finance the operation, programsand activities of the Sugar Regulatory Administration in pursuance of its charter objectives. > For this purpose, the proceed as herein provided shall be set aside to constitute a fund known as the Sugar Industry Research and Stabilization Fund which shall be paid out for the purpose herein stated.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-08-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING ALL AGRICULTURAL LANDS WITH NOT LESS THAN TEN PERCENT (10%) AND NOT MORE THAN THIRTY PERCENT (30%) PLANTED TREES FROM THE COVERAGE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6657, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The object of this measure is to protect our ecology and the future by requiring planting of more trees, even in agricultural lands. These trees would be able to provide for our lumber needs in the future and thus prevent logging in the forests. It gives the assurance that upon the full implementation of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform (CARP), these agricultural lands would not be barren lands instead would be potent source of forest resources.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2001-08-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PRIVATE-HOSPITA L DEVELOPMENT PLAN AND PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO PRIVATE HOSPITALS BY GRANTING THEM INCENTIVES
rows.abstract: Rationale: There are at least seventy percent (70%) privately owned hospitals around the country. These hospitals provide better services compared to government owned ones. > To help these private hospitals maintain and continue delivering quality service to our countrymen, this bill proposes a Private Hospital Development Plan which will be jointly formed with the Secretary of Health, proper government agencies and non-government organization. This plan shall oversee the much needed facilities, human resources and other needs of the private hospitals. This plan also grants tax incentives to qualified private hospitals only.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-08-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE LIABILITIES OF INDIRECT EMPLOYERS IN THEIR JOB CONTRACTING, COVERING OTHER BENEFITS DUE THEIR EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 106 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Among our country's labor force, those hired through job agencies are the most exploited, neglected, oppressed, and poorly paid. > This bill commands/direct s companies/emplo yers that workers hired through job contractors must receive all the benefits due them. However, if in any case the workers are not able to receive the benefits justly for them, they can likewise get their attention to the company they are working for redress.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-08

rows.author: D078
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 213, 215 AND 216 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, BY UPGRADING THE SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF LABOR ARBITERS AND THE COMMISSIONERS OF THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Labor Arbiters are judges, who are better equipped with training, experience and background to handle labor controversies, in the Philippines labor justice system. They adjudicate the very sensitive issues between labor and management. Since, they perform significant role in the maintenance of industrial peace and in the adjudication of justice in the workplace, it is fitting that Labor Arbiters enjoy equality in rank with the judges of the Regional Trial Courts. Appropriate retirement benefits must likewise be accorded them to enable them to enjoy the fruits of government service long after they have served it with their best years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-08

rows.author: C019
rows.title_full: AN ACT CURTAILING THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITIES OF RACKETEERS AND POWERFUL SYNDICATES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This piece of legislation proposes stronger measures against the pervasive and powerful criminal syndicates, racketeers and other socially and economically pernicious criminal organizations. It seeks to deprive these organized elements the operationsl fund for their activities. > Aside from securing criminal conviction of members of powerful crime and syndicates and their accomplises, this bill also aims to deny them the fruits of their illegal activities, on which they live lavish lifestyles.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-08-08

rows.abstract: "Enhances Rural-Agricultu re Program of 2001". This amendatory bill therefore ensures that credit is made available to small farmers and bottlenecks to developing the agricultural sector are addressed. Some of the important features of the bill areas follows: (1) Creation of the Rural Agricultural Development Council; (2) Expanded Conduit Network; and (3) Expanded Mode of Compliance.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR UNAUTHORIZED ALTERATION OF ELECTION RETURNS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any law to the contrary notwithstanding , any member of the Board of Election Inspectors or Board of Canvassers who tampers, increases, or decreases the votes received by a candidate in any election after the announcement of the results thereof in the polling place, unless so ordered by the Commission on Elections or a competent court, shall be criminally liable for serious election offense and if found guilty, shall: (1) Be punished with imprisonment of not less than six years and one day butnot more than twelve years; (2) Be dusqualified for holding public office; and (3) Be deprived of the right of suffrage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-08-08

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING CERTAIN POSITIONS IN THE BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE AND BUREAU OF CUSTOMS AS PART OF THE CONFIDENTIAL STAFF OF THE APPOINTING OFFICIALS IN SAID BUREAUS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to immunize BIR and Customs officers from graft and corrupt practices depriving the government of much needed income and revenues. At the same time those who betray the public trust may be more expeditiously removed from positions oftrust. A Board of Selection and Inquiry for each bureau will be created to handle the recruitment, selction and or removal of revenue and customs officers.

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY TO ANY GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE WHO HAS RENDERED AT LEAST TEN (10) YEARS CONTINUOUS GOVERNMENT SERVICE WITHOUT TAKING ANY CIVIL SERVICE EXAMINATION
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to grant government employees who have rendered continuous satisfactory service for at least ten (10) years a subprofessional or professional civil service eligibility, as the case may be, and shall qualify them for appointment to anyposition under the following classifications : Subprofessional Civil Service Eligibility: (1) Has rendered at least ten (10) years continuous and satisfactory service; and (2) Has completed at least two (2) years of college education leading to a college degree. Completion of at least 72 units in college or completion to a 2-year technical course with basic collegiate subjects, such as English and Mathematics, shall be considered equivalent to 2-year college education. Professional Civil Servicce Eligibility: (1) Has rendered at least ten (10) years continuous and satisfactory service; (2) Has completed a 4-year college education leading to a college degree; and (3) A second grade subprofessional civil service eligible.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-08

rows.author: B031
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AUTOMATIC MEMBERSHIP OF PROFESSIONALS TO THEIR RESPECTIVE ACCREDITED PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The State shall promote and protect various professional disciplines, unify and strengthen the bond amongst all professionals, and encourage their active involvement in organizations which serve as vehicles for nurturing the standard of practice of the profession thereby ensuring the contribution of professionals in uplifting the general welfare and development of the nation. In the pursuit of these obejectives, the State shall require the automatic membership of professionals to their respective accredited professional organization.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-08

rows.author: B031
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291 AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1146, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `REVISED GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE ACT OF 1977', AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill proposes that all years credited for initial retirement, resignation or separation for which corresponding benefits have been awarded, shall be included for purposes of computation of service in case an official or employee is reinstated in the government service with the option given to the said employee to choose under what law he will retire. However, this is subject to the condition that the benefits received upon initial separation or retirement prior to his reinstatement, shallbe deducted from the benefits he shall receive from his subsequent retirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-08-08

rows.author: B031
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING MEDICAL NEUTRALITY, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 169, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The physician's oath commands him to treat any person in distress regardless of the latter's creed, color, religion or nationality. If compliance to Presidential Decree would jeopardize his patient's life, then a physician has all the rights to rage against such instruction. > PD No. 169 required physicians and medical practitioners to report their treatment of any person for physical injuries to the nearest government health authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-08-08

rows.author: B031
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF RESPIRATORY THERAPY AND CREATING THE BOARD OF EXAMINERS FOR RESPIRATORY THERAPISTS, PROVIDING FOR ITS STRUCTURE AND ORGANIZATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The field of RESPIRATORY THERAPY encompasses a broad area of clinical expertise needing a thorough understanding of basic anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology and the physics of gases and a familiarity with the growing number of respiratory care devices required in caring for persons with pulmonary disorders such as asthma, acute respiratory failure with or without carbon dioxide retention, bronchitis, emphysema and other forms of obstructive and restrictive pulmonary diseases. > Recently, problems in the employment of such graduate have risen because of government requirements for licensed personnel as well as international accreditation's requirements for respiratory therapy practitioners.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-08

rows.author: D074
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE NATIONAL HOUSING AUTHORITY TO DEVELOP AND CONSTRUCT MASS HOUSING PROJECTS IN FOURTH, FIFTH, AND SIXTH CLASS MUNICIPALITIES IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: Rationale: The development and construction of housing units in the rural areas will channel investments to the countryside and will provide jobs to the unemployed particularly those in the construction sector. This will also generate economic activities therein such as in the procurement, delivery, and purchase of construction supplies and materials. Most of all, this will provide decent life to low-salaries members of the community who have been dreaming to have a house of their own.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2001-08-08

rows.author: D010
rows.title_full: AN ACT LOWERING THE COSTS OF MEDICINES AND HEALTH CARE IN THE PHILIPPINES BY EXEMPTING THE SALE, IMPORTATION, PROCESSING, REPACKING OR MANUFACTURING OF MEDICINES; PHARMACEUTICAL PRODUCTS; MEDICAL AND DENTAL AND HOSPITAL EQUIPMENT; AND RAW MATERIALSTO BE USED IN THE MANUFACTURE THEREOF, FROM ALL DUTIES AND TAXES
rows.abstract: Rationale: With the elimination of these duties and taxes, the costs of goods directly related to health care will be lowered and the manufacturers and distributors can then pass on the benefit to the Filipino consumer. This will eventually translate into a lower cost of health care for all Filipinos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-08

rows.author: D010
rows.title_full: AN ACT CLARIFYING ISSUES ON PARALLEL IMPORTATION AND DISTRIBUTION OF FOOD PRODUCTS AND MEDICINES IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: Importation into, and marketing in the Philippines of food products and medicines shall be allowed, regardless of whether or not the same is covered by any exclusive distributorship agreement between the manufacturer and its exclusive distributor, provided that the same passes through proper registration with the Bureau of Food and Drugs of the Department of Health, and with Bureau of Customs of the Department of Finance. > The act of importation into, and distribution in the Philippines of food products and medicines by persons or entities other then the exclusive distributor, shall not be considered as an act of unfair competition nor an infringement of the intellectual property rights of the latter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-08-08

rows.author: C089
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING AND REGULATING THE OPERATION OF CABLE TELEVISION IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The main objective of this bill is to promote and regulate the operation of the cable television industry within the country. This is in recognition of the fact that the delivery of cable television services to subscribers is impressed with public interest. This bill also aims to allow viable competition in the cable television industry to achieve and sustain its growth and to ensure that the same is responsbie to the needs and interests of the subscribers and the general public. Monopoly in the information and communication field must be discouraged, if not prohibited outright.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-08-08
